text:
sara: Heads-up — noticed rising egress costs on spot-backed clusters during noon burst. Thinking we should tweak scale-out trigger to be latency-aware, not queue-length only.

mike: Agreed. Queue depth -> bad signal for short lived spikes. Can we use p95 latency + inflight tokens as the primary trigger?

raj: We experimented w/ that. Worked but caused overprovisioning on flappy models. Added a short rolling window and surge cap to prevent cascade.

olivia: What did you set the surge cap to?

raj: `surge_cap: 15%` and `scale_out_cooldown: 45s` in the spot pool. Also a separate "hedge" on-demand pool at 5% baseline.

sara: Can you paste the config snippet?

raj: ```
autoscaler:
  mode: mixed
  spot_pool:
    trigger: p95_latency>120ms && queue>10
    surge_cap_pct: 15
    cooldown_s: 45
  on_demand_hedge:
    baseline_pct: 5
    max_burst_pct: 20
``` 

leo: Two notes: (1) p95 latency calc must exclude cold-starts or KV-cache-miss spikes, (2) if interruption rate > 2% prefer stricter surge cap or raise hedge baseline.

sara: How do we measure interruption rate in realtime? Cloud spot signal is noisy.

mike: We stream the provider preempt signals into metrics and compute rolling window. `interrupts_per_min_per_node` is our metric.

olivia: Also add a short "immune" window after scale-outs to avoid immediate scale-ins when capacity hasn't warmed: `scale_in_protect_s: 120`.

infra-bot: autoscaler: triggered scale_out of 8 nodes (spot) at 1779999000, reason: p95_latency=145ms > 120ms

sara: ok plan: raj will push config to staging, run 24h, mike will add dashboard for interrupt rate and p95 excluding cold starts, olivia to monitor cost delta. @raj @mike @olivia

mike: sounds good :thumbsup:

raj: I'll push today and ping results later.
